root_cause: ScrollController::jump_to dispatched only an Update, so a changed jump outside any activity bracket emitted no Start or End (Flutter jumpTo: goIdle, then Start/Update/End when pixels changed).
change: crates/incular-scroll/src/controller.rs jump_to: when no activity bracket is open and the offset changes, dispatch Start, Update, End in Flutter order. Inside an open bracket it still dispatches a bare Update and leaves the bracket to its owner (see limitations).
harness: scroll__controller__jump_activity_notifications: match (was DIVERGES: notifications.start/end 0 vs 1 at frame 2)
limitations: Flutter's goIdle also ends an open bracket on every jump (even an unchanged one). Ending the bracket was tried and reverted: it broke about 30 pinned gesture and fling takeover contracts in incular-widgets/tests/scroll_viewport_lists.rs. The narrower rule covers the reported case; in-bracket jump notification parity is not yet matched.
note: Confirmed before fixing: the twin diverged at frame 2 (start and end 1 in Flutter, 0 in Incular).

root_cause: jump_to clamped the requested offset to [0, max] before writing it, so an out-of-range jump landed on the edge at once. Flutter's jumpTo forces the raw pixels and then goBallistic(0) springs back.
change: crates/incular-scroll/src/controller.rs jump_to: an attached controller keeps the raw offset and sets pending_settle/springing_back. take_pending_settle builds ScrollPhysics::ballistic_simulation from the last published physics. crates/incular-scroll/src/physics.rs commit_extent_state keeps a springing position across unchanged republications and clears springing_back once in range. crates/incular-widgets/src/tree/interaction.rs start_scroll_animations starts the spring as an overscroll ScrollFlingDriver. Unattached controllers still clamp.
harness: scroll__controller__jump_clamp: first divergence now value.offset at frame 4 (64 ms) by 0.0021 (Flutter 97856.2010, Incular 97856.2031). The spring reproduces Flutter, but the value tolerance is 0.001, so the residual is float drift in the spring integration.
api_change: ScrollController::jump_to no longer clamps an attached controller. Callers that need the clamped value (layout corrections) use the new correct_to.
limitations: Only the default clamping spring is exercised by the twin. The bouncing spring and the spring when the viewport is reduced-motion are covered by the code path, not by a frame twin.
note: Confirmed before fixing: frame 3 Flutter 100000 vs Incular 1400.

root_cause: ScrollController had no way to state a starting offset; only restoration and deferred_jump_to set one.
change: crates/incular-scroll/src/controller.rs: with_initial_scroll_offset(offset) stores an InitialOffset applied on the first publication with a non-zero viewport, clamped to the extents (Flutter applyContentDimensions) and not persisted. Restoration takes precedence over it, and a deferred jump takes precedence over both (crates/incular-scroll/src/physics.rs commit_extent_state).
limitations: The precedence against PageStorage restoration is inherited from restoration (restored offset wins); it is not exercised by a twin.
note: Confirmed by reading: ScrollController::new took no initial offset.

root_cause: Bouncing physics emitted OverscrollNotification in two places: apply_physics reported the bounce amount for drags, and drive_unclamped reported it for bouncing ballistic steps. Flutter reports Overscroll only for amounts a clamping boundary condition removes.
change: crates/incular-scroll/src/physics.rs apply_physics: Overscroll only when boundary is Clamping. crates/incular-scroll/src/activity.rs drive_unclamped: Overscroll only when the last published physics is not bouncing. Clamping springs still report it, as Flutter's setPixels does.
harness: scroll__drag_overscroll__bouncing: overscroll notifications now match (Flutter 0, Incular 0). The remaining divergence is value.notifications.user_scroll (Flutter 1, Incular 0 at frame 3), which also diverges in every drag scenario and is outside this change.
limitations: Material RefreshIndicator and StretchingOverscrollIndicator consumed Overscroll under bouncing physics. They must now use the Update path, which refresh.rs already handles, and the stretch indicator is no longer driven by bouncing. Flutter behaves the same way, but this was not checked by a test in incular-material.
note: Confirmed before fixing: scenario overscroll notifications Flutter 0, Incular 32.

root_cause: PageController was a type alias of ScrollController, so there were no page-number operations, no initial page and no viewport fraction.
change: crates/incular-widgets/src/scrolling/scroll_views.rs: PageController is now a newtype that Derefs to ScrollController, with with_initial_page, with_viewport_fraction, initial_page, viewport_fraction, page() (Option, None before layout), jump_to_page, animate_to_page, next_page and previous_page. Page mapping uses Flutter's formulas via incular_scroll::pixels_for_page and page_for_pixels (crates/incular-scroll/src/controller.rs). Before layout, a page request is deferred (Flutter _pageToUseOnStartup) through ScrollController::defer_page. From<ScrollController> keeps existing callers working.
harness: scroll__page_view__fraction_initial_page: still match (4 frames). The twin uses deferred_jump_to, so it does not exercise the new API.
api_change: PageController changes from a type alias to a struct (derefs to ScrollController; PageController::new, restored and Default are kept). PageView::controller takes impl Into<PageController>.
limitations: Page math uses the controller's viewport fraction, not PageView::viewport_fraction. A fraction set only on the view is honored by layout but not by page(), jumpToPage or animateToPage. next_page/previous_page and animate_to_page were not exercised by a frame twin.
note: Confirmed by source reading: pub type PageController = ScrollController, with no page operations.

root_cause: PageView had no onPageChanged callback; the only workaround was a controller-level listener in the harness.
change: crates/incular-widgets/src/scrolling/scroll_views.rs: PageView::on_page_changed(callback). From<PageView> wraps the view in NotificationListener and calls the callback on depth-zero Update notifications when the rounded page changes (PageController::take_page_change, which is doc-hidden). The last reported page starts at the initial page, so mounting never reports (Flutter _lastReportedPage).
harness: scroll__page_view__fling_page_changed: page and page_changes match. Remaining divergence is probe.page0.present (Flutter false, Incular true from frame 44), which is cache retention, not the callback. The twin still uses the controller-listener workaround and was not edited.
limitations: The callback wiring through NotificationListener is not covered by an automated test; only the page-change decision is. The harness twin was not changed to use the new callback.
note: Confirmed before fixing: no PageView callback existed (source reading and scenario workaround).

root_cause: Scrollable.ensureVisible needs the target's rectangle in the coordinates of every ancestor scroll viewport. The tree has GlobalKey, but no keyed rectangle query and no ancestor-viewport walk.
limitations: Deferred: it needs a tree-level geometry query (keyed element to global rect, then an ancestor viewport walk with Flutter alignment and animation policy). That API does not exist yet, so it is larger than this pass.
note: Source reading only. rg for ensure_visible found nothing in incular-widgets or incular-scroll.

root_cause: ListWheel's last reported index started as None, so the first layout reported the item the wheel starts on as a change (Flutter seeds _lastReportedItemIndex with the initial item).
change: crates/incular-widgets/src/advanced_scrolling/wheel.rs layout_with_offset: seed last_selected_index from the first layout's selected item before reporting, so the starting item is not reported.
harness: scroll__list_wheel__selected_fling: frame 0 now matches (selected_changes 0). Remaining divergence starts at frame 3, where the drag does not scroll Incular (offset 0 vs Flutter 66.7). See limitations.
limitations: The drag does not scroll the wheel in the harness. That is a gesture or hit-test path issue, not the report, and it is the reason selected_changes diverges later.
note: Confirmed before fixing: frame 0 selected_changes Flutter 0, Incular 1.

root_cause: The retained tree laid wheel children out with measure = biggest(), so each child took the full viewport width and its cross-axis offset was 0. Flutter centres each child by its own width.
change: crates/incular-widgets/src/tree/layout/behavior/scrolling.rs wheel branch: after each child is laid out, its placement x = (viewport width - rendered width) / 2, using Tree::render_size. The headless path (crates/incular-widgets/src/advanced_scrolling/wheel.rs layout_with_measure) already centred from its measure.
harness: scroll__list_wheel__selected_fling: probe item0 x is now 250.0-550.0 (Flutter 250.5-549.5). The y and transform still differ because the drag does not scroll the wheel (see scroll-009).
limitations: The retained path places children correctly, but WheelLayout.untransformed_rect (used by WheelLayout::hit_test) still uses x = 0 for children laid out with the retained measure, so hit testing can disagree with paint. The test covers only the headless measure path. Hit-test alignment was not verified.
note: Confirmed before fixing: probe item0 x Flutter 250 to 550, Incular 0 to 300.
